subject: rstan::traceplot: Trouble with Arial font when saving to PDF

messages.author: 8b5528dd7856a600
messages.subject: rstan::traceplot: Trouble with Arial font when saving to PDF
parts:
While trying to rerun a script that worked in November on Rstan 2.12.1, I found that saving a traceplot to PDF now fails with "Error in grid.Call.graphics(L_text, as.graphicsAnnot(x$label), x$x, x$y, : invalid font type.” After some digging, it seems the rstan plotting theme now sets family=“Arial” but on my machine R only knows Arial by the name “ArialMT”.

A minimal example that doesn’t use Stan at all, just the theme:

library("ggplot2")
plt = ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt,mpg))+geom_point()
thm = get("theme", envir=rstan:::.rstanvis_defaults)

# Works as expected, plot uses Helvetica
ggsave("fontdemo_1.pdf", plt)

# Fails ("invalid font type"), leaves PDF with plot half-drawn
ggsave("fontdemo_2.pdf", plt + thm)

# Works, plot uses Arial
ggsave("fontdemo_3.pdf", plt + thm + theme(text=element_text(family="ArialMT")))

# Works iff you have extrafont correctly installed and set up
# and Arial present on your machine
library("extrafont")
loadfonts()
ggsave("fontdemo_4.pdf", plt + thm)

Discussion:
* Is a change in Rstan the appropriate place to fix this, or is there a pathology in my setup? If in Rstan, I'll open an issue.
* I tested the example above on OS X (10.11.6, running R 3.3.2) and Amazon Linux (4.4.41-35, running R 3.2.2). Same behavior on both except that my Amazon image has no Arial font for extrafont to find, so plot 4 fails there.
* I’m aware that font handling for PDFs is a messy topic in general, so I’m not sure what to recommend as a solution. Does “ArialMT” work on Windows?

—Chris
